exposure: protracted vacuum extraction (defined as vacuum duration > 15 min, > 6 pulls or > 2 cup detachments)
cohort: The study included all term, live-born infants in Sweden from 1999-2013, comprising cases diagnosed with neonatal intracranial hemorrhage after vacuum-assisted delivery and controls without this diagnosis.
finding: Protracted vacuum extraction was strongly associated with an increased risk of neonatal intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted OR 8.04, 95% CI 4.49-14.38) compared to extractions adhering to safety recommendations.
mod_finding: Protracted vacuum extraction, characterized by duration, number of pulls, or cup detachments exceeding safety recommendations, significantly increases the risk of neonatal intracranial hemorrhage.
